book_title: The First Epistle of John the Apostle.

verses.text: <sc>THAT</sc> vvhich vvas from the beginning, vvhich vve haue heard, vvhich vve haue seen vvith our eies, vvhich vve haue looked vpon, and our handes haue handled of the vvord of life:
( and the life vvas manifested: and we haue seen, and do testifie, and declare vnto you the life eternal vvhich was vvith the Father, and hath appeared to vs)
that vvhich we haue seen and haue heard, vve declare vnto you, that you also may haue societie vvith vs, and our societie may be with the Father and vvith his Sonne <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ.
And these things vve vvrite to you, that you may reioyce, and your ioy may be ful.
And this is the annuntiation vvhich vve haue heard of him, and declare vnto you, That <cr>[1]</cr> God is light, and in him there is no darkenesse.
If vve shal say that we haue societie vvith him, and vvalke in darkenesse: vve lie, and do not the truth.
But if we vvalke in the light, as he also is in the light: vve haue societie one tovvard an other, and <cr>[1]</cr> the bloud of <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ his sonne cleanseth vs from al sinne.
<cr>[1]</cr> If we shal say that vve haue no sinne, vve seduce our selues, and the truth is not in vs.
If vve confesse our sinnes: he is faithful & iust, for to forgiue vs our sinnes, and to cleanse vs from al iniquitie.
If we shal say that vve haue not sinned: vve make him a lier, and his word is not in vs.

chapters.summary: Good cause there is to beleeue the Apostles preaching. 5 And this is one point of their preaching, that to haue participation with God, we must not onely beleeue, but also abstaine from al mortal sinne, 8 though we al sinne venially.

verses.text: MY litle children, these things I write to you, that you sinne not. But & if any man shal sinne, vve haue an <na>[1]</na> caduocate vvith the Father, <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ the iust:

notes.text: c παράκλητον.

verses.text: and he is the propitiation for our sinnes: and not for ours only, but also for the vvhole vvorldes.
And in this vve know that vve haue knovven him, if vve obserue his commaundements.
He that saith he knovveth him, and keepeth not his commaundements: is a lier and the truth is not in him:
But he that keepeth his vvord, in him in very deede the charitie of God is perfited: in this vve know that vve be in him.
He that saith he abideth in him: ought euen as he walked, him self also to vvalke.
My deerest, I vvrite not a nevv commaundement to you, but an old commaundement which you had from the beginning. The old commaundement is the vvord vvhich you haue heard.
Againe <cr>[1]</cr> a nevv commaundement vvrite I to you, vvhich thing is true both in him and in you: because the darkenesse is passed, and the true light now shineth.
He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother: is in the darkenesse euen vntil novv.
<cr>[1]</cr> He that loueth his brother, abideth in the light, and scandal is not in him.
But he that hateth his brother: is in the darkenesse, and vvalketh in the darkenesse, and knovveth not vvhither he goeth, because the darkenes hath blinded his eies.
I write vnto you litle children, because your sinnes are forgiuen you for his name.
I write vnto you fathers, because you haue knovven him vvhich is from the beginning. I vvrite vnto you yong men, because you haue ouercome the vvicked one.
I vvrite to you infantes, because you haue knovven the Father. I write vnto you yong men, because you are strong, and the vvord of God abideth in you, & you haue ouercome the vvicked one.
Loue not the vvorld, nor those things vvhich are in the vvorld. If any man loue the vvorld, the charitie of the Father is not in him.
because <na>[1]</na> al that is in the vvorld, is the concupiscence of the flesh, & the concupiscence of the eies, and the pride of life, vvhich is not of the Father, but is of the world.

notes.text: all. How all sin and temptation proceed of these three, see S. Thomas Sum. 1. 2. quæst. 77. art. 5.

verses.text: And the vvorld passeth and the concupiscence thereof. But he that doeth the vvil of God, abideth for euer.
Litle children, it is the last houre, & as you haue heard, that <na>[1]</na> cAntichrist commeth: now there are become many antichristes: whereby vve knovv, that it is the last houre.

notes.text: c ὁ ἀντίχριςος.

verses.text: They vvent out from vs: but <na>[1]</na> they vvere not of vs. for if they had been of vs, they vvould surely haue remained with vs: but that they may be manifest that they are not al of vs.

notes.text: They were of vs for the time, that is, of and in the Church: otherwise they could not haue gone out. but they were not of the cōstāt sort, or of the elect & prędestinat: for then they had taried within, or returned before their death.

verses.text: But you haue <na>[1]</na> the cvnction from the Holy one, and knovv al things.

notes.text: χρῖσμα Chrisma. whereof Christ & Christians.

verses.text: I haue not written to you as to them that know not the truth, but as to them that know it: and that no lie is of the truth.
VVho is a lier, but he vvhich denieth that <sc>IESVS</sc> is not Christ? This is Antichrist vvhich denieth the Father and the Sonne.
Euery one that denieth the Sonne, neither hath he the Father. He that confesseth the Sonne, hath the Father also.
You, that vvhich you haue <na>[1]</na> heard from the beginning, let it abide in you. If that abide in you vvhich you haue heard from the beginning, you also shal abide in the Sonne & the Father.

notes.text: Keepe that firmely & constantly which you haue heard euen from the beginning, by the mouth of the Apostles: & not that only which you haue receiued by writing.

verses.text: And this is the promis vvhich he promised vs, life euerlasting.
These things haue I vvritten to you concerning them that seduce you.

And you, the vnction vvhich you haue receiued from him, let it abide in you. And you haue no neede that any man teache you: but as his vnction teacheth you of al things, and it is true, and it is no lie. And as it hath taught you, abide <na>[1]</na> cin him.

notes.text: or, in it.

verses.text: And now litle children abide in him: that vvhen he shal appeare, vve may haue confidence, and not be confounded of him in his comming.
If you know that he is iust, knovv ye that euery one also <na>[1]</na> vvhich doeth iustice, is borne of him.

notes.text: We see it is Apostolical doctrine, that men may do or worke iustice, and that so doing they be iust by their workes, proceding of Gods grace, & not by faith or imputation onely.

chapters.summary: If any sinne mortally, he must not despaire. 3 To know God rightly, is not to beleeue onley, but to keepe his commaundements: 7 and that this is no new doctrine, but the very primitiue, though a new life it is. 9 Therfore he that beleeueth must also loue his brethren: 12 and that men must not loue the world, but doe that which God willeth. 18 Many are gone out of the Church and become Seducers, al the ministers of Antichrist: but true Christians must continue in their old faith, considering the reward, and that they neede not goe to schole to any Heretike, the Holy Ghost himself being the scholemaster of the Church. 29 he doth earnestly inculcate iustice and good workes.

verses.text: <sc>SEE</sc> vvhat maner of charitie the Father hath giuen vs, that vve should be named and be <na>[1]</na> the sonnes of God. For this cause the world doth not knovv vs, because it hath not knovven him.

notes.text: Not by nature, as Christ is: but by grace and adoption.

verses.text: My deerest, novv we are the sonnes of God: & it hath not yet appeared vvhat we shal be. VVe know that when he shal appeare, we shal be like to him: because vve shal <na>[1]</na> esee him as he is.

notes.text: How we shal see God, & be like vnto him in the next life, see S. Augustine ep. 111. 112. & li. 12. de ciuit. Dei c. 29.

verses.text: And euery one that hath this hope in him, <na>[1]</na> sanctifieth him self, as he also is holy.

notes.text: This teacheth vs that man sanctifieth him self by his free wil working together with Gods grace. S. Augustine vpon this place.

verses.text: Euery one that committeth sinne, committeth also iniquitie: and sinne is iniquitie.
And <cr>[1]</cr> you knovv that he appeared to take away our sinnes: <cr>[2]</cr> and sinne in him there is none.
Euery one that abideth in him, sinneth not: and euery one that sinneth, hath not seen him, nor knowen him.
Litle children, let no man seduce you. He that doeth iustice, is iust: euen as he also is iust.
<cr>[1]</cr> He that committeth sinne, is of the deuil: because the deuil sinneth from the beginning. For this, appeared the Sonne of God, that he might dissolue the vvorkes of the deuil.
Euery one that is borne of God, committeth not sinne: because his seede abideth in him, and he can not sinne because he is borne of God.
In this are the children of God manifest, and the children of the deuil. Euery one that is not iust, is not of God, and he that loueth not his brother.
<cr>[1]</cr> because this is the annuntiation, vvhich you haue heard from the beginning, <na>[2]</na> That you loue one an other.

notes.text: The Epistle for S. Polycarpus, Ian. 26.

verses.text: Not as <cr>[1]</cr> Cain, vvho was of the vvicked, and killed his brother. And for vvhat cause killed he him? Because his vvorkes vvere vvicked: but his brothers, iust.
<na>[1]</na> Maruel not brethren, if the vvorld hate you.

notes.text: The Epistle vpon the 2. Sunday after Pentecost.

verses.text: We knovv that we are translated from death to life, because vve loue the brethren. He that loueth not, abideth in death.
VVhosoeuer hateth his brother: is a murderer. And you knovv that no murderer hath life euerlasting abiding in him self.
<cr>[1]</cr> In this vve haue knovven the charitie of God, because he hath yelded his life for vs: and vve ought to yeld our liues for the brethren. ⊢
<cr>[1]</cr> He that shal haue the substance of the vvorld, and shal <na>[2]</na> see his brother haue neede, and shal shut his bovvels from him: hovv doth the charitie of God abide in him?

notes.text: Ia. 2, 15. · Euery man is bound to giue almes according to his abilitie, when he seeth his brother in great necessitie.

verses.text: My litle children, let vs not loue in word, nor in tongue, but in deede and truth. ⊢
In this vve knovv that vve are of the truth: and in his sight vve shal persuade our hartes.
For if our hart do reprehend vs: God is greater then our hart, and knovveth al thinges.
My deerest, if our hart do not reprehend vs, vve haue confidence tovvard God.
And <cr>[1]</cr> vvhatsoeuer we shal aske, vve shal receiue of him: because vve keepe his commaundementes, and doe those thinges vvhich are pleasing before him.
And <cr>[1]</cr> this is his commaundement, that we beleeue in the name of his Sonne <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ: and <na>[2]</na> loue one an other, as he hath giuen commaundement vnto vs.

notes.text: Lest any man should thinke by the wordes next before, onely faith in Christ to be commaunded or to please God, he addeth to faith the commaundement of charitie or loue of our neighbour.

verses.text: And <cr>[1]</cr> he that keepeth his commaundementes, abideth in him, and he in him. And in this vve knovv that he abideth in vs, by the Spirit vvhich he hath giuen vs.

chapters.summary: It is not for the sonnes of God, to sinne mortally, but for the sonnes of the Diuel, wherby they are knowen one from an other, & not by onely faith. 11 True faith it is, that we also loue our brethren, giuing both our life and substance for them. 19 Such vnfeined loue may haue great confidence before God. 23 because the keeping of his commaundements doth much please him, which consist in faith and charitie.

verses.text: MY deerest, beleeue not euery spirit, but proue the spirites if they be of God: because many false prophetes are gone out into the vvorld.
In this is the spirit of God knovven. euery spirit that confesseth <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ to haue come in flesh, is of God:
and euery spirit that dissolueth <sc>IESVS</sc>, is not of God: and this is <na>[1]</na> cantichrist, of vvhom you haue heard that he commeth, and now he is in the vvorld.

notes.text: c τὸ τοῦ ἀντίχριςτου.

verses.text: You are of God, litle children, and haue ouercome him. because greater is he that is in you, then he that is in the world.
They are of the vvorld: therfore of the vvorld they speake, and the vvorld heareth them.
VVe are of God. <cr>[1]</cr> He that knovveth God, heareth vs. he that is not of God, heareth vs not. in this vve know the spirit of truth, and the spirit of errour.
My deerest, let vs loue one an other: because charitie is of God. And euery one that loueth, is borne of God, & knovveth God.
<na>[1]</na> He that loueth not, knovveth not God: because God is charitie.

notes.text: The Epistle vpon the first Sunday after Pentecost.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> In this hath the charitie of God appeared in vs, because God hath sent his only-begotten sonne into the vvorld, that vve may liue by him.
In this is charitie: not as though vve haue loued him, but because he hath loued vs, and sent his sonne a propitiation for our sinnes.
My deerest, if God hath so loued vs: vve also ought to loue one an other.
<cr>[1]</cr> God <na>[2]</na> no man hath seen at any time. If vve loue one an other, God abideth in vs, and his charitie in vs is perfited.

notes.text: No man in this life, nor with corporal eyes, can see the proper essence or substance of the Deity. See S. August. ad Paulin. de videndo Deo. cp. 112.

verses.text: In this vve know that vve abide in him, and he in vs: because he of his Spirit hath giuen to vs.
And vve haue seen, and doe testifie, that the Father hath sent his Sonne the Sauiour of the vvorld.
VVhosoeuer shal confesse that <sc>IESVS</sc> is the Sonne of God, God abideth in him, and he in God.
And vve haue knovven and haue beleeued the charitie, vvhich God hath in vs. God is charitie: and he that abideth in charitie, abideth in God, and God in him.
In this is charitie perfited vvith vs, that vve may haue confidence in the day of iudgement: because as he is, vve also are in the vvorld.
Feare is not in charitie: but perfect charitie casteth out feare, because feare hath painefulnes. and he that feareth, is not perfect in charitie.
Let vs therfore loue God, because God first hath loued vs.
If any man shal say, that I loue God: and hateth his brother, he is a lier. For he that loueth not his brother vvhom he seeth: God vvhom he seeth not, hovv can he loue?
<cr>[1]</cr> And this commaundement vve haue from God: that he vvhich loueth God, loue also his brother. ⊢

notes.text: The Church only, not every private man, hath to prove and discern spirits.

chapters.summary: We may not beleeue al that boast of the spirit, but trie them. Whether they teach Catholike articles of the faith (namely the incarnation of Christ:) whether their doctrine be not worldly, and them selues disobedient hearers of the Apostles. 7 We must loue one an other, considering the exceding loue of God in sending his sonne to saue vs. 17 An argument of perfect charitie is, if we haue nothing in our conscience to feare in the day of Iudgement. 19 And an argument that we loue God is, if we loue our brethren.

verses.text: <sc>WHOSOEVER</sc> beleeueth that <sc>IESVS</sc> is Christ, is borne of God. And euery one that loueth him vvhich begat: loueth him also vvhich vvas borne of him.
In this vve knovv that vve loue the children of God: vvhen as we loue God, and keepe his commaundementes.
For this is the charitie of God, that vve keepe his commaundementes: <cr>[1]</cr> and his commaundementes are not heauy.
<na>[1]</na> Because al that is borne of God, ouercommeth the vvorld. and this is the victorie vvhich ouercommeth the vvorld, our faith.

notes.text: The Epistle vpon Dominica in albis or Low Sunday.

verses.text: VVho is he <cr>[1]</cr> that ouercommeth the vvorld, but he that beleeueth that <sc>IESVS</sc> is the sonne of God?
This is he that came by vvater and bloud <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ: not in vvater only, but in vvater and bloud. And it is the Spirit vvhich testifieth, that Christ is the truth.
For there be three vvhich giue testimonie in heauen, the Father, the VVord, and the Holy Ghost. and these three be one.
And there be three vvhich giue testimonie in earth: the spirit, vvater, and bloud. `and these three be one'.
If we receiue the testimonie of men, the testimonie of God is greater. because this is the testimonie of God vvhich is greater, that he hath testified of his sonne.

<cr>[1]</cr> He that beleeueth in the sonne of God, hath the testimonie of God in him self. ⊢ He that beleeueth not the Sonne, maketh him a lier: because he beleeueth not in the testimonie vvhich God hath testified of his sonne.
And this is the testimonie, that God hath giuen vs life euerlasting. And this life is in his sonne.
He that hath the Sonne, hath life. he that hath not the sonne of God, hath not life.
These thinges I vvrite to you, that you may knovv that you haue eternal life which beleeue in the name of the sonne of God.
And this is the confidence which vve haue toward him: that, <cr>[1]</cr> vvhatsoeuer vve shal aske according to his vvill, he heareth vs.
And <na>[1]</na> cvve knovv that he heareth vs whatsoeuer vve shal aske: vve knovv that vve haue the petitions vvhich vve request of him.

notes.text: c or, if we know

verses.text: He that knoweth his brother to sinne a sinne not to death, let him aske, and life shal be giuen him, sinning not to death. There is a sinne to death: for that I say not that any man aske.
Al <na>[1]</na> ciniquitie, is sinne. And there is a sinne <na>[2]</na> <alt>`to death</alt>'.

notes.text: c ἀδικία
`not to death.

verses.text: VVe know that euery one vvhich is borne of God, sinneth not: But the generation of God preserueth him, and the vvicked one toucheth him not.
VVe knovv that vve are of God, and the vvhole vvorld is set in vvickednesse.
And vve know that the sonne of God commeth: and he <cr>[1]</cr> hath giuen vs vnderstanding, that vve may know the true God, & may be in his true sonne. This is the true God, & life euerlasting.
My litle children, keepe your selues from Idols. <na>[1]</na>Amen.

notes.text: ἀπὸ τῶν ἐιδώλων.

chapters.summary: They that loue God, must loue his natural sonne IESVS, and his sonnes by adoption, and keepe his commaundements, which to the regenerate are light. 4 But not, vnles they continue in the Catholike faith, namely of this article, that IESVS is the sonne of God, and therfore able to giue vs life euerlasting, 14 and al our petitions, 16 and our praiers for al our brethren that sinne not vnto death, dying in their mortal sinnes by impenitence. Last of al, he warneth them not to communicate with Idols.

intros.title: THE ARGUMENT OF S. JOHN'S THREE EPISTLES.
intros.text: OF S. John was said in the Argument before his Gospel. Now here follow his three Epistles: one to all Catholics (though [1] some ancients do call it, Ad Parthos :) the other two being very short, unto a certain Lady, & to one Gaius. The effect of all is, to witness unto them the certainty of the Catholic faith, and to exhort them to continue still in it: also to love the Catholic Church, and so, neither to become heretics, nor Schismatics: but rather to avoid all such, as the forerunners of Antichrist, and to remember, that Catholics need not to go to school to any such Masters, having at home in the Catholic Church, the doctrine of the Holy Ghost himself, who was given to the Church visibly in the beginning, to lead her into all truth, and to continue with her for ever. Therefore he saith: [2] That which you have heard from the beginning, let it abide in you. Likewise a little after. v. 27. and ep. 2. v. 6. This is the commandment, that as you have heard from the beginning, you walk in the same, because many seducers are gone out into the world. and v. 8. & 9. And not only thus in general, but also in particular he expresseth the points which the heretics did then call in question. Some were about Christ himself. For they denied that JESUS is Christ, that he is the very son of God, that he is incarnate. Ep. 1. c. 2. v. 22. and Ep. 2. v. 7. And against such it was that he wrote his Gospel also, as he there signifieth. Ioh. 20. v. 31. Other points are about our justification, against only faith, and for good works, as also S. Aug. noted [3] , whose words were cited before. Hereupon he saith: If we say we have society with God, and walk in darkness, we lie. Ep. 1. c. 1. Again, [4] He that saith he knoweth God, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar. Again, This is the charity of God, that we keep his commandments, and his commandments are not heavy. Finally, Children let no man seduce you, he that doth justice, is just, even as he is just. Ep. 1. c. 3. v. 7. 8. 9. likewise c. 2. v. 29. and indeed in all the three Epistles throughout, he doth inculcate good works and keeping the commandments, against the heresy of only faith.

notes.text: * Higinus ep. 1. to. 1. Concil. August. li. 2. Evang. quaest. q. 39.
De fid. & op. c. 14.
